It still duplicates Add and makes an explicitly out-of-scope retry change, but A directly violates the required public signature and adds forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["B implements the exact required signature: Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead exposes opts ...UploadFileOption, creating an incompatible API.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile exactly as required. A expands the helper with NewForm and routes Upload through that new machinery.","B preserves existing FilesOption query and request-option handling in Upload. A invents WithUpload* options and association form fields, despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields and requiring unchanged FilesOption behavior.","B tests empty filename, nil content, source-reader failure, multipart field/filename/content, and retry behavior. A has a stronger non-seekable-source retry assertion, but omits a visible Upload source-reader-error test and focuses tests on its unauthorized options API."],"risks_a":["The public Upload signature violates the frozen contract and would reject existing FilesOption values expected by callers.","Adds numerous WithUpload* association APIs and NewForm multipart machinery expressly outside scope.","Upload bypasses Add and duplicates its response handling; it also drops existing FilesOption query behavior by using nil query parameters and a separate option system entirely differently from the required API surface and handling path. Corrections would require material API and implementation rework, so this is not merge-ready under the contract."],"risks_b":["Upload still calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request construction, decoding, and missing-data handling.","The RawClient buffering change is explicitly outside the requested scope and changes behavior for every non-native io.Reader, including memory use, read-error timing, streaming behavior, and potentially reader-closing semantics.","The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a genuinely streamed/non-replayable source and only counts attempts instead of verifying multipart content on each attempt."]}
